title: Development Discourses
description: A curated library of research papers, books, and grey literature for development practitioners in South Asia.

items.title: Supporting learning in and out of school: Experimental evidence from India
items.content_text: A cross-cutting trial across 200 villages in Assam. Neither the in-school pedagogy component nor the community study groups moved learning alone; together they raised maths by 0.11 SD and language by 0.09 SD. An argument about complementarity rather than about either component. Published online on 21 August 2026; the publisher assigns it to the January 2027 issue (volume 184), which is why the year reads 2027.

authors.name: Martina Björkman Nyqvist, Andrea Guariso

items.title: Women in the Platform Economy: Descriptive Evidence from Drivers in India and Indonesia
items.content_text: Uses survey and administrative data from two-wheeler driving and delivery platforms in India and Indonesia. Women are 0.8 percent of drivers in India and 1.5 percent in Indonesia, work fewer hours than men, earn 6 to 8 percent less per hour in India and report more harassment.

authors.name: Achyuta Adhvaryu, Levina Adiputri, Valentina Brailovskaya, Priyanka Dua, Jenny Susan John, Pratibha Joshi, Terry Muthahhari, Rivandra Royono, Jack Thunde

items.title: Where Are Pakistan’s Out-of-School Children? Mapping Accessibility of Schooling Using Satellite Data and Machine Learning Methods with an Application to the 2022 Floods
items.content_text: Combines satellite imagery, the population census, government school censuses and public location data on private schools to map where Pakistan's out-of-school children are in relation to schools. It documents more than 72,700 private schools alongside more than 137,000 public schools and applies the method to the 2022 floods.

authors.name: Umar Saif, Amer Hasan, Ayesha Tahir, Koen Geven, Mohsen Ali, Aliza Masood, Muhammad Abdul Rahman, Sheena Fazili

items.title: The Limits of Government Outsourcing: Property Tax Re-Assessments in India
items.content_text: Reports an experiment in Chennai, India, in which neighborhoods were randomly selected to have property tax assessments done by contracted private firms in place of government tax inspectors. Government inspectors produced almost double the increase in tax revenue and more accurate assessments.

authors.name: Esther Duflo, Rema Hanna, Benjamin A. Olken, Shreya Tandon

items.title: The Emergence of the Poverty–Mental Health Gradient and the Great Pakistan Earthquake of 2005
items.content_text: Uses data from 126 villages collected four years after the 2005 Pakistan earthquake. Among people nearest the fault line, mental health improves by 0.12 standard deviations per log unit of consumption, while beyond 20 km there is no relationship between consumption poverty and mental health.

authors.name: Tahir Andrabi, Benjamin Daniels, Jishnu Das

items.title: The City Through Her Eyes: Gender-Based Harassment in Public Spaces in Urban India
items.content_text: Surveys over 4,000 women recruited in public spaces in New Delhi and Bengaluru about harassment. It reports that 65 percent of women in New Delhi and 29 percent in Bengaluru experienced harassment in public spaces in the past year, and that measured prevalence is sensitive to questionnaire design.

authors.name: Lori A. Beaman, Seema Jayachandran, Anisha Sharma

items.title: Targeting, Personalization, and Engagement in an Agricultural Advisory Service
items.content_text: Reports a series of experiments on how to target calls from an agricultural advisory service that serves over one million farmers in rural India. Targeted policies raised engagement by up to 8 percent when evaluated on data from the design period, but realized gains were substantially smaller when the policies were implemented in later weeks.

authors.name: Susan Athey, Shawn Cole, Shanjukta Nath, Jessica Zhu

items.title: Survival or Growth? Nepal’s Microenterprise Landscape and the Case for a Differentiated Policy Approach
items.content_text: Uses two new enterprise surveys from 2024-25 and 2025 to compare informal and formal microenterprises in urban Nepal for the first time. It finds deep structural differences between the two groups and that only a small share of informal firms could benefit from formalizing, and it recommends livelihood and social protection support for most informal firms with targeted productivity support for the few with growth potential.

authors.name: Jumana Alaref, Laurine Martinoty, Aishwarya Patil, Mohamed Ihsan Ajwad, Jasmine Rajbhandary

items.title: Responding to Floods in Pakistan with Adaptive Social Protection: How to Keep an Inundated Country Afloat
items.content_text: Reviews the response to the 2022 floods in Pakistan, which affected about 33 million people. It finds that the government used several instruments but that coverage of relief support remained limited, and it identifies ways to build an adaptive social protection system on the existing social protection system.

authors.name: Zaineb Majoka, Yash Dhuldhoya

items.title: Mobile money, and the welfare of women and youths in fragile states: Evidence from Mozambique
items.content_text: 900 households from the 2019 FinScope survey in a post-conflict, climate-exposed setting. Welfare gains run through active usage, not account ownership. The authors state plainly that their instrument cannot be fully tested, which is worth more than the point estimate.

authors.name: Lwanga Elizabeth Nanziri et al.

items.title: Measuring the Impact of Impact Measurement
items.content_text: Reports a randomized controlled trial of an impact measurement intervention among high-growth social enterprises in India. Treated firms show nearly twice the revenue growth of control firms and raise nearly twice as much capital. In a companion experiment, early-stage investors respond to quantified impact metrics but not to generic qualitative impact statements.

authors.name: Emanuele Colonnelli, Timothy McQuade, Natalia Rigol, Benjamin N. Roth

items.title: Impact of Cash Transfers on Child Poverty Among School-aged Refugee Children: Evidence from Uganda
items.content_text: Alkire-Foster multidimensional poverty combined with propensity score matching in Kyaka II. A 7 per cent effect, which the authors read as cash alone being insufficient against child multidimensional poverty rather than as a success.

authors.name: Emmanuel Keith Kisaame, Susan Namirembe Kavuma, Edward Bbaale

items.title: Household Preferences for Women’s Employment: A Field Experiment in Bangladesh
items.content_text: Randomly assigns a six-week job to either the husband or the wife in households in Bangladesh. Women's work improves their own wellbeing but not their husbands', while men's work improves both partners' wellbeing. One year later, households in which the woman had worked are more likely to prefer that she take a new job.

authors.name: Yueh-ya Hsu, Reshmaan N. Hussam, Erin M. Kelley, Gregory Lane

items.title: Fintech and Savings in African Countries: The Case of Mobile Money
items.content_text: Harmonised FinScope surveys from Malawi, Tanzania and Uganda across 2013, 2017 and 2021, instrumented on distance to the nearest agent. The contribution is the decomposition: mobile money moves saving onto digital platforms and away from banks and ROSCAs rather than simply raising the amount saved.

authors.name: Claudia Chilundo, Hermine Vedogbeton

items.title: Evaluating Alternative Approaches to Small Area Estimation of Poverty with Survey and Census Data
items.content_text: Uses five rounds of Mexican and Brazilian census extracts to test how accurately different models and estimation methods produce small area estimates of poverty from survey and census data. Models with household-level or village-level predictors tend to be more accurate than models with area-level predictors only, and no single approach dominates across all contexts.

authors.name: Hai-Anh H. Dang, Minh Do, Partha Lahiri, Melany Gualavisi, David Newhouse, Talip Kilic, Peter Lanjouw, Roy Van der Weide

items.title: Doing Better at Doing Good: Lessons from a Bayesian Meta-Analysis After 20 Years of Poverty Graduation Programs
items.content_text: A Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis of 49 studies of poverty graduation programs. Monthly consumption rises by 38 USD PPP (11 percent) and income by 28 USD PPP (15 percent). Lower-cost programs tend to be more cost-effective, and programs implemented from 2016 onward have higher benefit-cost ratios than earlier ones.

authors.name: Samantha Carter, Edward Jee, Dean Karlan, Patrick Premand

items.title: Disability and educational outcomes in Nepal: Evidence from the 2019 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey
items.content_text: Uses a nationally representative sample of 7,824 children aged 5 to 17 from the 2019 Nepal Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey. It relates functional disability to whether a child ever attended school, current grade level and being in the appropriate grade for age, controlling for age, gender, location, mother's education and household wealth.

authors.name: Prashant Acharya

items.title: Digital personalised learning to improve literacy and numeracy outcomes: a randomised controlled trial in Kenyan pre-primary classrooms
items.content_text: 1,955 pre-primary learners across 291 Kenyan government schools over 13 months, 0.53 SD from baseline. Worth reading for the decay after midline, which the authors attribute to running out of suitable content rather than to the method failing.

authors.name: Louis Major et al.

items.title: Digital Land Rights and Rural Credit Access: Lessons from Village Habitation (Abadi) Land Titling in India
items.content_text: Studies India's SVAMITVA program, which issued property cards for rural residential homesteads. Difference-in-differences estimates across 42,000 villages in Madhya Pradesh show that issuing property cards created sustained land and credit market activity where there had been none, in remote communities as much as in those near bank branches.

authors.name: Klaus W. Deininger, Daniel Ayalew Ali, Hari K. Nagarajan, Abhiman Das, Parth Hirpara

items.title: Bringing legislation to life: Navigating intersectional barriers in implementing the Sindh Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities Act (2018) for the healthcare of children with disabilities
items.content_text: A qualitative study in four districts of Sindh, Pakistan, based on 40 key informant interviews, on how the health provisions of Sindh's 2018 disability Act are implemented for children with disabilities. It identifies weak governance, limited coordination between sectors and the absence of a sanctioned budget for inclusive health as gaps.

authors.name: Muhammad Asim, Waqas Hameed, Sara Rotenberg, Dalia Chowdhury, Abid Lashari, Munazza Gillani, Abdul Ghaffar, Hannah Kuper

items.title: Beyond access: clean energy use in low-income and middle-income countries
items.content_text: Makes the measurement argument plainly: SDG 7's binary indicators overstate health and equity gains because they cannot see fuel stacking, dynamic consumption or the gendered burden of polluting fuels.

authors.name: Annelise Gill-Wiehl et al.

items.title: Association between water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) practices and childhood stunting in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.content_text: 16 studies, 36,574 children. Water quality, water accessibility and sanitation facility type are associated with lower stunting odds; drinking water source, household treatment, toilet access and safe disposal of child faeces are not. Observational, and the authors say so.

authors.name: Frengki Prabowo Saputro Wijayanto et al.

items.title: Air Pollution and Student Learning in Pakistan
items.content_text: Estimates the effect of sustained exposure to fine particulate matter on primary-school learning in rural Punjab, Pakistan, using longitudinal test score data and satellite pollution estimates. Using upwind crop-residue fires as an instrument, it finds that higher pollution during the school year significantly slows learning, with larger effects in mathematics than in language subjects.

authors.name: Saher Asad, A. Patrick Behrer, Martin Philipp Heger, Monica Yanez Pagans

items.title: Access is Not Enough: How Smartphone Ownership Shapes Digital Services Use in Low- and Middle-Income Countries
items.content_text: Uses data from 71 countries to study how smartphone ownership affects the use of digital services in low- and middle-income countries. Ownership raises the likelihood of using services such as learning, government services and job search by 34 percentage points, but gender gaps persist because of affordability, digital skills and social norms.

authors.name: Yuna Liang, Sylvan Rene Herskowitz, Antonio Martins-Neto, Sharada Srinivasan

items.title: Yield Gains from Balancing Fertilizer Use
items.content_text: Uses data on a large sample of rice fields in three states of eastern India to test whether a more balanced use of fertilizer, measured as the ratio of potash to nitrogen, raises yields and revenues. Fertilizer balance is instrumented with the relative distances from villages to the nearest urea plant and the nearest international port.

authors.name: Julian Arteaga, Klaus Deininger

items.title: World mental health today: latest data
items.content_text: A 64-page WHO report that updates the evidence on mental health epidemiology, economic consequences and gaps in public mental health. It states that over one billion people live with a mental disorder and that most remain underserved.

authors.name: World Health Organization

items.title: World Development Report 2025: Standards for Development
items.content_text: The World Bank's World Development Report for 2025. It describes standards as the hidden infrastructure of modern economies and examines how developing countries can deal with increasingly stringent international standards produced by globalization and rapid technological change.

authors.name: World Bank

items.title: When Water Runs Out: Adaptation to Gradual Environmental Change in Indian Agriculture
items.content_text: Uses differences in geology that affect the rate of groundwater depletion across 40 villages in Gujarat, India, as a natural experiment. Greater water scarcity leads to declines in irrigated agriculture and more migration to cities among dominant socio-economic groups only, with no evidence of substantial investment in water-efficient technologies or in human capital.

authors.name: Ram Fishman, Meha Jain, Avinash Kishore

items.title: Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) Factors and the Incidence of Communicable Diseases in Urban Bangladesh: Evidence from Municipal Areas
items.content_text: PLOS NTDs study finding that nearly one in four participants in urban Bangladesh reported communicable diseases, with diarrhoea most common and poor hand hygiene showing the strongest disease association.

authors.name: Md Nuruzzaman Khan, Raaj Kishore Biswas, Shuva Das

items.title: Water and Sanitation in Indian Cities: Knowledge Framework for Promoting Sustainable and Bankable Water Supply, Sanitation, and Solid Waste Management
items.content_text: A World Bank and Asian Development Bank framework for modernizing water supply, sanitation and solid waste management in 100 large Indian cities. It draws on assessments of infrastructure and service performance across these cities and on detailed diagnostics of 10 of them, and reports progress in infrastructure coverage alongside remaining gaps in service quality, efficiency and sustainability.

authors.name: World Bank, Asian Development Bank (ADB)

items.title: Two Settlements, Two Diverging Paths: Jobs and Labor Market Outcomes for the Displaced Rohingya Population
items.content_text: Compares labor market outcomes for displaced Rohingya in the Cox's Bazar camps and on Bhasan Char, using harmonized survey data from 2022 and 2023. It reports that informal economic activity has grown in both settlements despite legal prohibitions on formal employment, and that only about one-third of working-age people were employed in the year before the survey.

authors.name: World Bank, UNHCR

items.title: Towards Resilient and Prosperous Cities in India
items.content_text: Makes the case for investment in climate-resilient cities in India. The report states that the urban population is expected to double from 480 million in 2020 to 951 million by 2050 and that more than half of the urban infrastructure, buildings and services needed are still to be built, which gives cities a chance to plan for resilience.

authors.name: World Bank Group

items.title: The impact of a participatory intervention to improve learning outcomes and reduce school-based discrimination and community stigma in primary rural schools of Afghanistan: A cluster control randomized trial
items.content_text: 83 schools across three Afghan provinces, 2,519 children. Life skills, self-efficacy and reading literacy all improve, effects rise with dose, and girls gain more than boys. One of the few learning trials run in an active crisis setting.

authors.name: Jean-Francois Trani et al.

items.title: The false optimism of electrification: why universal electricity access has not delivered urban energy transformation in South Africa
items.content_text: Argues that counting grid connections measures proximity to a wire, not access to energy services, and that households in un-serviceable settlements are permanently excluded by design. Directly relevant to anyone reading SDG 7 progress figures.

authors.name: Charlotte Lemanski et al.

items.title: The Impact of Shock-Responsive Social Cash Transfers: Evidence from an Aggregate Shock in Kenya
items.content_text: Kenya's shock-responsive scheme during the pandemic, on informal-economy households. Less income loss, less food scarcity, and fewer distress sales of productive assets — but only where payment cycles were pooled and transfers vertically scaled.

authors.name: Christoph Strupat, Emmanuel Nshakira-Rukundo, Arndt Reichert

items.title: The Global Findex Database 2025: Connectivity and Financial Inclusion in the Digital Economy
items.content_text: The fifth edition of the Global Findex, based on nationally representative surveys of about 145,000 adults in 141 economies. It adds new series on mobile phone ownership, internet use, digital safety and the frequency of financial transactions, and reports on how adults use phones, the internet and financial accounts to save, borrow and make payments.

authors.name: Leora Klapper, Dorothe Singer, Laura Starita, Alexandra Norris

items.title: The Evolution of Local Participatory Democracy in Nepal
items.content_text: Traces the development of Nepal's participatory institutions over about 50 years in three phases, ending with the 2015 federal constitution, which granted local autonomy. It examines how far these institutions were induced by external interventions and how far they grew from indigenous practices, and reports five findings on how reforms widened citizens' influence over local decisions.

authors.name: Thaneshwar Bhusal, Michael G Breen, Vijayendra Rao

items.title: The Effects of Taxes and Transfers on Inequality and Poverty in Pakistan
items.content_text: Applies the Commitment to Equity methodology to taxes, social spending and subsidies in Pakistan for fiscal year 2019. It finds that the fiscal system raised the national poverty headcount by about two percentage points, had a muted effect on inequality, and left only the poorest decile as net recipients in cash terms.

authors.name: Beenish Amjad, Haydeeliz Carassco, Moritz Meyer

items.title: Talk Therapy and Human Capital in Adolescence: Evidence from Nepal
items.content_text: Reports a randomized therapy intervention for 1,707 Nepali adolescents at risk of dropping out of school. Among those who took part, therapy reduced psychological distress and improved emotional regulation, but these gains did not raise school attendance or cognitive performance.

authors.name: Eric V. Edmonds, Priya Mukherjee, Nikhilesh Prakash, Nishith Prakash, Shwetlena Sabarwal

items.title: State of Social Protection Report 2025: The 2-Billion-Person Challenge
items.content_text: Documents that 2 billion people in low- and middle-income countries remain uncovered by social protection, with three out of four people in low-income countries receiving no support and current growth rates requiring 18 years to achieve full coverage.

authors.name: World Bank

items.title: Sri Lanka Country Climate and Development Report
items.content_text: The World Bank Group's Country Climate and Development Report for Sri Lanka. It estimates potential economic losses of 3.3 to 3.5 percent of GDP by mid-century from heat stress on labor productivity, lower agricultural yields and more intense flooding in urban and rural areas.

authors.name: World Bank Group

items.title: South Asia Development Update, October 2025: Jobs, AI, and Trade
items.content_text: The World Bank's October 2025 economic update for South Asia. It projects regional growth of 6.6 percent in 2025 and 5.8 percent in 2026, reports that about 15 percent of South Asian workers are in jobs where artificial intelligence strongly complements human labor, and discusses how carefully sequenced tariff cuts could encourage private investment and job creation.

authors.name: World Bank

items.title: South Asia Development Update, April 2025: Taxing Times
items.content_text: The World Bank's April 2025 economic update for South Asia. It argues that higher revenue mobilization is a prerequisite for stronger fiscal positions in most South Asian countries and reports that the region's economies face larger tax gaps than the average emerging market and developing economy.

authors.name: World Bank

items.title: Socioeconomic Inequalities in Access to Maternal Healthcare in South-Asian Countries: A Systematic Review
items.content_text: Systematic review of 55 studies from India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, and Pakistan showing that maternal healthcare access is linked to economic status, education, and women's autonomy in patriarchal family structures.

authors.name: Parveen Ali, Rubab Zahra, Shehla Naeem, Sana Waqas

items.title: Scalable Targeting of Social Protection: When Do Algorithms Out-Perform Surveys and Community Knowledge?
items.content_text: Compares proxy means-testing, community nominations and a machine learning approach based on mobile phone records as ways to identify poor households for transfers in Bangladesh. Proxy means-testing is the most accurate, but algorithmic targeting becomes more cost-effective for national-scale programs in which large numbers of households must be screened.

authors.name: Emily Aiken, Anik Ashraf, Joshua Blumenstock, Raymond Guiteras, Ahmed Mushfiq Mobarak

items.title: Reclaiming Momentum Towards Prosperity: Pakistan's Poverty, Equity, and Resilience Assessment
items.content_text: A World Bank poverty assessment for Pakistan. It reports that poverty fell from 64.3 percent in 2001 to 21.9 percent in 2018 and is projected to have risen to 25.3 percent by 2023/24 after COVID-19, economic instability, floods and high inflation. It calls for policy reforms to address structural imbalances.

authors.name: World Bank

items.title: Progress on household drinking-water, sanitation and hygiene 2000-2024: Special focus on inequalities
items.content_text: The 2025 report of the WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme. Between 2000 and 2024, 2.2 billion people gained access to safely managed drinking water and 2.8 billion gained safely managed sanitation, but progress has been uneven, and the number of people without safely managed drinking water has increased in urban areas and in low-income countries.

authors.name: World Health Organization, UNICEF

items.title: Nepal Country Economic Memorandum
items.content_text: A World Bank report on Nepal's growth opportunities. It analyses growth trends across three periods, policies to increase the economic benefits of migration, the effect of exchange rate dynamics and trade policies on merchandise exports, and the potential of hydropower and digitalization.

authors.name: World Bank

items.title: Moving toward Universal Health Coverage with a National Health Insurance Program: A Scoping Review of Experiences in Eleven Low- and Lower-Middle-Income Countries
items.content_text: Assesses strategies adopted by low- and lower-middle-income countries with a national health insurance scheme to expand UHC, examining variations in progress across eleven countries.

authors.name: Katya Galactionova, Elizabeth Kalesha, Abena Asumadu-Sakyi, Fabrizio Tediosi

items.title: Methodological Guidelines on Assessing Household Disability: Related Costs and Their Implication for Participation
items.content_text: Guidelines from the World Bank and UNICEF on how to assess the costs that households face because of disability. They distinguish direct costs, such as assistive products and higher spending on everyday goods and services, from indirect costs, such as reduced education or employment for persons with disabilities and their caregivers.

authors.name: World Bank, UNICEF
